mainTopic: Offerings before the משכן: which animals were allowed, whether בני נח brought שלמים, and when יתרו came
overview: The גמרא explains a ברייתא about the offerings brought before the משכן was set up. Back then, males, females and even blemished animals could be offered, because animals were compared to birds. An animal missing a limb was still not allowed, and רבי אלעזר learns this from 'ומכל החי'. After a long back-and-forth, the גמרא concludes that a טריפה is excluded through 'אתך', because the animals had to be like נח, who was whole. 'לחיות זרע' then teaches that the animals had to be able to reproduce. Next the גמרא explains how נח knew which animals were 'pure': either the תיבה took them in, or they came on their own. It then discusses whether בני נח brought שלמים or only עולות. This becomes a מחלוקת tied to the question of when יתרו came, before or after מתן תורה. The amud ends with three תנאים explaining what news brought יתרו: the war with עמלק, מתן תורה (with the story of the kings and בלעם), or קריעת ים סוף.

steps.title: Why males, females and blemished animals were allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's ruling that males and females, unblemished and blemished animals could be offered. The reason is that animal was compared to bird, and birds have no requirement to be male or unblemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Males and females, unblemished and blemished' — this follows what the Master said: being unblemished and being male are required for animals, but not for birds. And in the story of נח, animal is compared to bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from a ברייתא and explains where that ruling comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, birds never need to be male or unblemished (תמות וזכרות), but animals do. In the פסוק about נח's sacrifices, animals and birds are placed side by side. That comparison (היקש) gives animals the same easy status as birds, so before the משכן was set up, male or female, blemished or unblemished animals were all fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared or linked by the Torah (a היקש)

phrases.english: Males and females, unblemished and blemished —
this is as the Master said:
being unblemished and being male apply to animals,
but being unblemished and being male do not apply to birds.
And animal was compared to bird.
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the Torah's rules, animals had the same status as birds, so males, females and blemished animals were all allowed.

steps.title: Blemished is allowed, but missing a limb is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא's words 'unblemished and blemished' still exclude an animal missing a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Unblemished and blemished' — this comes to exclude an animal missing a limb, which was not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit on the ברייתא: a blemish is fine, but a missing limb is not. This sets up the next step, which gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish (מום) is a flaw, but a missing limb (מחוסר אבר) is a much bigger lack. The ברייתא said 'blemished' and not more, so a missing limb stays disqualified even for בני נח.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a blemish with a missing limb. For בני נח a blemish was fine, but a missing limb was not.

phrases.english: Unblemished and blemished —
this comes to exclude one missing a limb, which was not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished animal was allowed, but one missing a limb was not.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source for excluding a missing limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר derives from 'ומכל החי' that בני נח may not offer an animal missing a limb. The Torah wants an animal whose main limbs are all 'alive'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: From where do we know that an animal missing a limb is forbidden to בני נח? The פסוק says 'And from every living thing of all flesh.' The Torah is saying: bring an animal whose main limbs are alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a פסוק as the source for the rule in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'החי' (the living) is read as 'whole and alive in all its limbs.' So an animal missing a limb does not count, and it may not be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of נח, meaning all non-Jews

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know that one missing a limb
is forbidden to the descendants of Noah?
The verse states: "And from every living thing of all flesh" —
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:19

phrases.english: The Torah said:

phrases.aramaic: הָבֵא בְּהֵמָה שֶׁחַיִּין רָאשֵׁי אֵיבָרִין שֶׁלָּהּ.
phrases.english: Bring an animal whose main limbs are alive.
phrases.notes: 'Alive' here means whole, with no main limb missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנַּיִן לִמְחוּסַּר אֵבֶר שֶׁנֶּאֱסַר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the exclusion in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That an animal missing a limb is forbidden to בני נח

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק excludes a טריפה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'ומכל החי' might be excluding a טריפה rather than an animal missing a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the פסוק comes to exclude a טריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's reading by suggesting a different use for the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה has a fatal injury and will not live, so 'the living' could fit it even better. If the פסוק is used up on טריפה, there is no source left for מחוסר אבר.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury

phrases.english: But perhaps it comes to exclude a tereifa?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's use of 'ומכל החי' for מחוסר אבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'living' could more naturally exclude a טריפה, which will not live, so the פסוק might not be teaching about a missing limb.

steps.title: טריפה comes from 'לחיות זרע'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule for טריפה is learned from 'לחיות זרע', so 'ומכל החי' is free to teach about a missing limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule is learned from 'to keep seed alive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving טריפה its own separate source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals in the תיבה had to be able to keep their kind going, and a טריפה cannot. Since טריפה already has a source, 'ומכל החי' teaches that an animal missing a limb is excluded, and רבי אלעזר's derivation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep seed alive (to keep the species going)

steps.whatToRemember: For בני נח: males, females and blemished animals are fine, but a מחוסר אבר is excluded ('ומכל החי'). Here טריפה is learned from 'לחיות זרע', but the גמרא revises this. In the end (step 13) טריפה is learned from 'אתך', and 'לחיות זרע' (step 15) requires animals that can reproduce.

phrases.english: That is derived from "to keep seed alive."
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source: the other case has its own פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ומכל החי' might be needed to exclude a טריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: טריפה is learned from 'לחיות זרע', so 'ומכל החי' excludes a מחוסר אבר.

steps.title: What about the view that a טריפה can give birth?
steps.stepSummary: The previous answer works only for the view that a טריפה cannot give birth. According to the view that it can, 'לחיות זרע' does not exclude a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer is fine for whoever holds a טריפה cannot give birth. But for whoever holds a טריפה can give birth, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 5. That answer only works according to one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said 'לחיות זרע' (to keep seed alive) excludes a טריפה, because a טריפה cannot have babies. But there is an opinion that a טריפה can give birth. According to that opinion, 'לחיות זרע' does not exclude a טריפה, so we need another source.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (but there is a problem with the other view)
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
What is there to say? (How do you answer?)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
a טריפה cannot give birth,
but according to the one who says
a טריפה can give birth —
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵיפָה אֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵיפָה יוֹלֶדֶת – מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 5's source for excluding a טריפה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'לחיות זרע' to exclude a טריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That source depends on the view that a טריפה cannot give birth. Under the opposing view, it excludes nothing.

steps.title: 'With you' means animals similar to נח
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אתך' teaches that the animals must be like נח, meaning whole and not a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'with you', meaning animals that are like you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a different word in the פסוק: 'אתך' (with you).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the animals had to be 'with you', they had to resemble נח. נח was not a טריפה, so a טריפה animal is excluded. This works even for the view that a טריפה can give birth.

phrases.english: Doesn't the verse say: 'with you' —
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:19

phrases.english: meaning ones that are similar to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source from the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'לחיות זרע' there is no source excluding a טריפה for the view that it can give birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אתך' excludes a טריפה, because the animals must resemble נח.

steps.title: Maybe נח himself was a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the animals must be like נח, maybe נח was a טריפה, and then 'אתך' would not exclude anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe נח himself was a טריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from 'אתך' only works if נח was whole. If נח was a טריפה, 'like you' would not rule out a טריפה animal at all.

phrases.english: But perhaps נח himself
was a טריפה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If נח was a טריפה, 'similar to you' would include a טריפה instead of excluding it.

steps.title: נח is called 'תמים' (whole)
steps.stepSummary: The תורה calls נח 'תמים', which shows he was physically whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written about him 'תמים' (whole).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק calls נח 'תמים', meaning whole and complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תמים' is read as describing נח's body: he had no defect. So he was not a טריפה.

phrases.english: 'Whole' is written about him.
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נח might have been a טריפה.

steps.title: Maybe 'תמים' means perfect in his ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'תמים' might describe נח's behavior, not his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he was whole in his ways?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: 'תמים' could be praise of נח's character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'תמים' means perfect in his conduct, it says nothing about his body. Then he might still have been a טריפה.

phrases.english: But perhaps he was whole in his ways?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'תמים' in Step 9.

steps.title: His goodness is already covered by 'צדיק'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק already calls נח 'צדיק', so 'תמים' must add something about his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Righteous' is written about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נח's good behavior is already described by the word 'צדיק'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. Since 'צדיק' covers his conduct, 'תמים' must be about his physical wholeness.

phrases.english: 'Righteous' is written about him.
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, בראשית 6:9. 'Righteous' already covers his good conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Avoiding a double meaning in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צדיק' already means good conduct, so 'תמים' refers to his body.

steps.title: Maybe the two words describe two kinds of goodness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'תמים' could mean perfect in his ways and 'צדיק' could mean righteous in his deeds. Then neither word describes his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps 'whole' means in his ways, and 'righteous' means in his deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Both words could be about character, each in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each word praises a different part of נח's character, neither one is extra. Then there is still no proof that נח's body was whole.

phrases.english: But perhaps 'whole' means in his ways,
and 'righteous' means in his deeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תמים' must refer to the body.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each word can describe a different part of his character, so neither one is extra.

steps.title: Logic proves נח was not a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: If נח were a טריפה, 'like you' would mean only טריפות may enter the ark and healthy animals may not. That makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think נח was a טריפה, would God tell נח: bring in ones like you, but do not bring in healthy ones?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the word-reading and proves its point with simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתך' means the animals must be like נח. If נח were a טריפה, the ark would allow only טריפה animals and keep out healthy ones, which is absurd. So נח was whole, and 'אתך' excludes a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you think so)

steps.whatToRemember: A טריפה is excluded through 'אתך': the animals in the ark had to be like נח, and נח was certainly whole.

phrases.english: If it enters your mind
that נח himself was a טריפה,
would He have said to נח:
bring in ones like you,
but do not bring in whole ones?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּנֹחַ גּוּפֵיהּ טְרֵיפָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 with logic instead of word-reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the other option is absurd
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נח might have been a טריפה, so 'אתך' would prove nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is absurd that only טריפות would be allowed in, so נח was whole and 'אתך' excludes a טריפה.

steps.title: Then why do we need 'לחיות זרע'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'אתך' already excludes a טריפה, the גמרא asks what 'לחיות זרע' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we learn it from 'with you', why do I need 'to keep seed alive'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תורה needs the words 'לחיות זרע' if 'אתך' already does the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה should teach something. If 'אתך' excludes a טריפה, 'לחיות זרע' seems unnecessary for that purpose.

phrases.english: And since we derive it from 'with you',
why do I need 'to keep seed alive'?
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דְּנָפְקָא לַן מֵ״אִתָּךְ״, ״לְחַיּוֹת זֶרַע״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 13's conclusion that 'אתך' excludes a טריפה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'לחיות זרע' teach, now that it is not needed to exclude a טריפה?

steps.title: 'לחיות זרע' excludes old or castrated animals
steps.stepSummary: From 'אתך' alone we might think the animals were just company, so even old or castrated ones would do. 'לחיות זרע' teaches that they had to be able to reproduce.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that 'with you' means just for company, so even an old or castrated animal is fine. That is why the פסוק says 'to keep seed alive'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'לחיות זרע' teaches a new rule: the animals had to be able to have offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתך' alone could suggest the animals were only there to keep נח company. In that case an old or castrated animal would be fine, as long as it was not a טריפה. 'לחיות זרע' adds that each animal had to be able to have babies.
steps.whatToRemember: Each word has its own job. 'אתך' excludes a טריפה, and 'לחיות זרע' excludes animals that cannot reproduce, such as old or castrated ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא's rule that no word in the תורה is extra. When one word covers a law, the other word must teach something new.

phrases.english: You might have said:
'with you' means merely for company,
so even an old one, even a castrated one would do;
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The word 'לחיות זרע' is what teaches us that they must be able to reproduce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לחיות זרע' excludes animals that cannot reproduce, such as old or castrated ones, which 'אתך' alone might have allowed as companions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אתך' excludes a טריפה, and 'לחיות זרע' requires animals able to reproduce.

steps.title: Before the משכן, only pure animals were offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: offerings came from pure animals, not impure ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pure animals, but not impure ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא it has been explaining. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that before the משכן, only טהורין animals could be offered and טמאין animals could not. This clause is the target of the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Pure ones, but not impure ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the same ברייתא, after the discussion of 'תמים' and 'אתך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משכן, offerings could come only from pure animals, not impure ones.

steps.title: Were there pure and impure animals back then?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea: the categories of pure and impure only came with the Torah, so how could they exist in נח's time?
steps.simpleTranslation: Were there really impure and pure animals at that time?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It asks how there could be 'pure' and 'impure' animals before the Torah was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of which animals are טהור and which are טמא come from the Torah, which was given long after נח. So it seems strange to say that נח picked 'pure' animals.

keyTerms.meaning: And were there really…? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: And were there impure and pure ones
at that time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הֲווֹ טְמֵאִין וּטְהוֹרִין בְּהַהִיא שַׁעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the clause just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that only pure animals were offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pure and impure are Torah categories, so they did not exist yet in נח's time.

steps.title: 'Pure' means animals never used for a sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן explains that 'pure' means animals that were never involved in a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: from those that no sin had been done with.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן answers the challenge. In נח's time, 'pure' did not mean kosher. It meant an animal that had not been used for a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes what 'pure' means in this story. It is not the later Torah category. It describes animals that stayed clean of sin. So the ברייתא makes sense even before מתן תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin was done with them

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
From those with which no sin had been done.
phrases.notes: He means animals that had never been used to commit a sin. Those are the 'pure' ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by giving 'pure' a different meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Pure' means kosher species, which did not exist as a category yet.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Pure' means animals that no sin was ever done with.

steps.title: How did they know which animals were involved in sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how נח and his sons could tell which animals had been used for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the last answer. How could anyone tell which animals had a sin done with them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something like that cannot be seen by looking at an animal. So the new meaning of 'pure' needs a way of knowing which animals fit it.

phrases.english: From where did they know?
phrases.notes: 'They' means נח and his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי יונתן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How נח could tell which animals were never used for a sin.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the תיבה took in only the pure ones
steps.stepSummary: נח passed the animals in front of the תיבה. The ones it took in were pure, and the ones it did not take in were impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: he passed them in front of the ark. Any that the ark took in was known to be pure. If the ark did not take them in, they were known to be impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב חסדא's teaching. The תיבה itself sorted the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח did not need to know each animal's history. The animals the תיבה accepted were pure, and the ones it refused were impure.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with what רב חסדא said

phrases.english: It is like what Rav Ḥisda said.
As Rav Ḥisda said:
He passed them in front of the ark;
any that the ark took in –
it was known that it was pure;
if the ark did not take them in –
it was known that they were impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תיבה took in the pure animals and refused the impure ones.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the pure animals came by themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns from the פסוק 'והבאים' that the animals came on their own, so only the pure ones arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says, 'And those that came, male and female.' This means those that came on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a second answer to how נח knew. He reads a פסוק to mean that the animals came on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'והבאים,' 'those that came,' shows the animals arrived by themselves. נח did not have to sort them, because only the right animals came. This is a different way of knowing than רב חסדא's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said,
the verse says:
"And those that came, male and female" –
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:16

phrases.english: those that came on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, different from רב חסדא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the fitting animals came to the תיבה on their own, as the word 'והבאים' shows.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to how נח knew which animals were 'pure': רב חסדא says the תיבה took in only the pure ones, and רבי אבהו says only the pure ones came on their own.

steps.title: Everything offered was an עולה, so no שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that all offerings were עולות, and infers that שלמים were not brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: And all were offered as עולות. עולות, yes; שלמים, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and draws an inference from it. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that before the משכן, everything brought was an עולה. That seems to mean שלמים were not brought at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offerings, burned completely on the מזבח
Peace offerings, partly eaten by the owners

phrases.english: The Master said:
And all were offered as burnt offerings.
Burnt offerings, yes; peace offerings, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משכן, all offerings were עולות, which seems to mean no שלמים were brought.

steps.title: The פסוק says שלמים were offered at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference with a פסוק saying שלמים were offered at הר סיני, before the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And they slaughtered peace offerings of oxen to ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from the ברייתא with a פסוק. That פסוק describes שלמים being offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מתן תורה, before the משכן was built, the Jews brought שלמים. So it cannot be true that only עולות were offered before the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But it is written:
"And they slaughtered peace offerings of oxen to the Lord"!
phrases.notes: שמות 24:5. This happened at הר סיני, before the משכן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference that no שלמים were brought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that שלמים were offered before the משכן.

steps.title: Correct the wording: עולות and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא's wording to say that offerings were עולות and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: All were offered as עולות and שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. It now includes שלמים too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was not trying to rule out שלמים. With the corrected wording, it fits the פסוק about שלמים at סיני.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
All were offered as burnt offerings [and peace offerings.
phrases.notes: The square bracket starts words that the corrected text adds. They keep going into the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא by correcting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא (אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only עולות were offered before the משכן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both עולות and שלמים were offered before the משכן.
steps.whatToRemember: Because of the פסוק about סיני, the ברייתא is corrected: before the משכן, both עולות and שלמים were offered.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says only burnt offerings were brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying that before the משכן no שלמים were brought, only עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'But not peace offerings, only burnt offerings'? That means burnt offerings yes, peace offerings no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording it just fixed in step 24. It brings a different ברייתא that clearly says שלמים were NOT brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the גמרא said offerings before the משכן were both עולות and שלמים. This new ברייתא says the opposite: only עולות. So we now have two sources that seem to argue.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: But peace offerings, no,
only burnt offerings.
phrases.notes: This closing square bracket ends the added words that started in the step before.

phrases.english: Burnt offerings, yes; peace offerings, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֲבָל שְׁלָמִים לָא, כִּי אִם עוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected reading from step 24 by using a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected wording that both עולות and שלמים were offered before the משכן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא states directly that only עולות were brought, which contradicts including שלמים.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows the view that בני נח did not bring peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the second ברייתא follows one side of a מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows the one who says that בני נח did not bring peace offerings. As it was said: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא argue. One says בני נח brought peace offerings, and one says they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות follow two different opinions. It names the מחלוקת behind them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is not a mistake. It reflects a real מחלוקת about whether בני נח ever brought שלמים. The ברייתא that says 'only עולות' follows the opinion that they did not.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says
the descendants of נח, meaning all people before מתן תורה and the non-Jewish nations

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא here does not tell us which of the two אמוראים holds which view. It only says 'one says' and 'one says'.

phrases.english: It is like the one who says they did not offer
peace offerings, the descendants of נח.
As it was stated: רבי אלעזר
and רבי יוסי בר חנינא argue.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: קֵרְבוּ שְׁלָמִים בְּנֵי נֹחַ,
phrases.english: One says: The descendants of נח offered peace offerings,
and one says: They did not offer them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא קֵרְבוּ שְׁלָמִים בְּנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by linking each ברייתא to a different side of a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources follow different opinions (תנאי היא style answer through an אמוראים dispute).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must agree, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that says 'only עולות' follows the view that בני נח did not bring שלמים.

steps.title: Source for the view that בני נח brought peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The view that בני נח brought שלמים learns it from הבל, who offered 'the fat' of his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says בני נח brought peace offerings? Because it is written: 'And הבל, he also brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat.' Which offering has its fat put on the מזבח, but not all of it? You must say: this is a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first opinion and gives a פסוק about הבל as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely, so the פסוק would not need to say 'fat' for it. Only a שלמים has just its fat burned while the meat is eaten. So the mention of fat shows הבל brought a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: הבל, son of אדם, counted here among the early generations
the fats of an animal that are burned on the מזבח
you must say, it must be

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says
the descendants of נח offered peace offerings?
As it is written: 'And הבל, he also brought
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:4

phrases.english: from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat.'

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁחֶלְבּוֹ קָרֵב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: What is something whose fat is offered on the altar,
but not all of it is offered on the altar?
You must say: this is a peace offering.
phrases.notes: With a שלמים, only the fats go on the מזבח and the meat is eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר קֵרְבוּ שְׁלָמִים בְּנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for the first side of the מחלוקת from step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that בני נח brought שלמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 4:4, where הבל brought 'from their fat,' which fits only a שלמים.

steps.title: Source for the view that בני נח did not bring peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The other view learns from 'Awake, north, and come, south' that the nations offered only in the north, meaning only עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says they did not bring them? Because it is written: 'Awake, north, and come, south.' The nation whose offerings are only in the north will be pushed away, and the nation whose offerings are in the north and the south will come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the second opinion: a פסוק from שיר השירים read as being about the nations and כלל ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולות must be slaughtered in the north side of the עזרה, while שלמים can be slaughtered anywhere, even the south. The nations are called 'north' because they brought only עולות. ישראל is called 'north and south' because they bring both עולות and שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: awake. The דרשה reads it as 'be shaken off'
will be shaken off, pushed away

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא קֵרְבוּ?
phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says they did not offer them?
As it is written: 'Awake, north, and come, south.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:16

phrases.english: The nation whose deeds are in the north will be shaken off,
phrases.notes: 'Deeds' here means offerings. עולות are slaughtered only in the north part of the courtyard.

phrases.english: and the nation whose deeds are
in the north and in the south will come.
phrases.notes: This is ישראל, who also bring שלמים, and שלמים can be slaughtered even in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא קֵרְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second side of the מחלוקת, parallel to step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that בני נח did not bring שלמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 4:16, read as contrasting the nations (north only, meaning עולות) with ישראל (north and south, meaning עולות and שלמים).

steps.title: How does the second view explain הבל's 'fat'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the opinion that בני נח did not bring שלמים deals with the פסוק 'and from their fat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the Master too, isn't it written: 'and from their fat'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second opinion with the first opinion's own פסוק about הבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 used 'from their fat' to prove הבל brought a שלמים. If the second opinion says בני נח never brought שלמים, it has to explain that פסוק some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to the Master too

phrases.english: And for the Master too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the one who says בני נח did not bring שלמים.

phrases.english: 'and from their fat'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the proof from step 27 and uses it against the opinion from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that בני נח did not bring שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about הבל mentions fat, and burning only the fat fits a שלמים, not an עולה.

steps.title: 'Their fat' means the fattest animals
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that 'מחלביהן' means הבל chose the fattest of his animals, not that he burned only their fats.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means from the fattest of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the word 'fat' differently. It means 'the best and fattest animals,' not the fat parts of an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'חלב' means 'the choicest animals,' the פסוק no longer proves that only the fats were burned. So הבל could have brought a whole עולה, and the second opinion still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת whether בני נח brought שלמים. One side learns from הבל's 'fat' that they did. The other side learns from 'north and south' that they brought only עולות, and reads הבל's 'fat' as 'the fattest animals.' That is why one ברייתא says only עולות were brought.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one word ('חלב') can be read as a technical term (the fats of an offering) or as a general description (the best animals). The whole מחלוקת depends on that reading.

phrases.english: From the fattest of them.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. It just stresses 'of them,' meaning the animals themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 by reinterpreting the key word of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מחלביהן' means the fats of the offering, which proves a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מחלביהן' means the fattest, choicest animals, so it does not prove a שלמים.

steps.title: How does the other side explain 'Awake, north'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the opinion that בני נח DID bring שלמים and asks how it deals with the פסוק 'עורי צפון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master too: isn't it written 'Awake, north'?
steps.whatsHappening: Until now we asked questions on the side that says בני נח did not bring שלמים. Now the גמרא asks the other side: what do you do with 'עורי צפון'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, 'עורי צפון' was used to show that the nations offered only in the north, which means only עולות. The side that says בני נח brought שלמים must explain this פסוק some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Master too, meaning the other opinion in the מחלוקת
'Awake, north', a פסוק in שיר השירים

phrases.english: And the Master too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the one who holds בני נח did bring שלמים.

phrases.english: 'Awake, north'!
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended one side's reading of 'מחלביהן', the גמרא now challenges the other side with the opposing פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that בני נח brought שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'עורי צפון' was read to mean the nations offered only in the north, which means only עולות, so how can this view say they brought שלמים?

steps.title: The north wind verse is about the ingathering of exiles
steps.stepSummary: That פסוק is not about the nations' offerings at all. It describes קיבוץ גלויות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about the ingathering of the exiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this side reads 'עורי צפון' as being about the Jewish exiles coming back from north and south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק is read as being about קיבוץ גלויות, it no longer says anything about where the nations' offerings were brought. So this side is free to say בני נח brought שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The gathering of the Jewish exiles back to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: That verse is written about the ingathering of the exiles.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עורי צפון' describes where the nations brought their offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: It describes קיבוץ גלויות, so it teaches nothing about the offerings of בני נח.

steps.title: משה asked פרעה for זבחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that בני נח did not bring שלמים: before מתן תורה, משה asked פרעה for 'זבחים ועולות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'And משה said: You too must give into our hand זבחים and עולות, and we will offer them to ה׳ our God'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא goes back to attack the side that says there were no שלמים before the Torah. It uses משה's words to פרעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זבחים' usually means שלמים. משה said this in מצרים, long before מתן תורה. That seems to show שלמים were brought before the Torah was given.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offerings that are fully burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
'And Moshe said: You too
must give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings
and we will offer them to ה׳ our God'!
phrases.notes: שמות 10:25

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה גַּם אַתָּה תִּתֵּן בְּיָדֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending both sides once, the גמרא brings a new challenge against the side that says בני נח did not bring שלמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that בני נח did not bring שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה asked for 'זבחים', meaning שלמים, before מתן תורה. So שלמים were offered before the Torah was given.

steps.title: זבחים were for eating, עולות for offering
steps.stepSummary: The 'זבחים' in משה's request were animals to eat, not שלמים. Only the עולות were for offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The זבחים were for eating, and the עולות were for offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the פסוק into two parts. The זבחים were food, and only the עולות were for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זבח' can just mean an animal slaughtered for food. Read that way, 'וְעָשִׂינוּ לַה׳' goes only on the עולות, so the פסוק does not prove that שלמים were offered.

phrases.english: The 'zevachim' were for eating,
phrases.notes: Here זבחים just means animals slaughtered for food.

phrases.english: and the burnt offerings were for offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זבחים' here means animals for food. Only the עולות were offered.

steps.title: יתרו brought an עולה and זבחים
steps.stepSummary: Another challenge: יתרו took 'עולה וזבחים' for God, which seems to be real שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'And יתרו, משה's father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק against the view that there were no שלמים before the Torah. This time it is about יתרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יתרו, the 'זבחים' cannot be explained away as food, because they were taken for God. So it looks like a non-Jew offered שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: משה's father-in-law, who joined the Jewish people in the מדבר

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
'And Yitro, Moshe's father-in-law, took
a burnt offering and sacrifices'!
phrases.notes: שמות 18:12. That פסוק goes on to say these were 'for God', so they were real offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 34, the גמרא brings a stronger פסוק that cannot be read as food.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that בני נח did not bring שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יתרו offered 'זבחים' to God, which means שלמים. That shows שלמים were offered by a non-Jew.

steps.title: יתרו's offering came after the Torah was given
steps.stepSummary: The יתרו story happened after מתן תורה, when שלמים were already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about the time after the giving of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יתרו brought his offerings after מתן תורה. So the story does not teach what happened before the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about whether שלמים existed BEFORE מתן תורה. If יתרו came after, his זבחים fit the new Torah system and prove nothing about בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: The giving of the Torah at הר סיני

steps.confusionAlert: In the חומש, the יתרו story appears before the פרשה of הר סיני. The גמרא's answer means the story is not written in time order.

phrases.english: That verse, about after the giving of the Torah,
is what it is written about.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא לְאַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing when the event took place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יתרו's offering happened before מתן תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It happened after מתן תורה, so it says nothing about the time before the Torah.

steps.title: But what about the view that יתרו came before the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The answer about יתרו works only for one view. What about the view that יתרו came before מתן תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says יתרו came after the giving of the Torah. But for the one who says יתרו came before the giving of the Torah, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weak spot in the last answer. Not everyone agrees that יתרו came after מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 depended on the יתרו story being after מתן תורה. If someone holds it was before, the פסוק again seems to show שלמים before the Torah, and the question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says
But for the one who says

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
Yitro came after the giving of the Torah;
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but for the one who says
Yitro came before the giving of the Torah,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the answer in step 36 depends on one side of a separate מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 36 (יתרו came after מתן תורה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some hold יתרו came before מתן תורה. For them, יתרו's זבחים still show שלמים before the Torah.

steps.title: The dispute about when יתרו came
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source showing there really is a מחלוקת about when יתרו arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: the sons of רבי חייא and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says יתרו came before the giving of the Torah, and one says יתרו came after the giving of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: This line backs up the question in step 37. It shows that the view 'יתרו came before מתן תורה' really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sides argue about when יתרו came. Since one side puts יתרו before מתן תורה, the answer of step 36 cannot work for everyone. This sets up the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the giving of the תורה
After the giving of the תורה

phrases.english: As it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי;
phrases.english: the sons of Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: יִתְרוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה,
phrases.english: one says Yitro came before the giving of the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: יִתְרוֹ אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה.
phrases.english: and one says Yitro came after the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion mentioned in step 37's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether יתרו came before or after מתן תורה.

steps.title: Whoever puts יתרו before the Torah holds בני נח brought שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The view that יתרו came before מתן תורה simply holds like the side that בני נח did bring שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says יתרו came before the giving of the Torah holds that בני נח did bring שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 37 by linking the two arguments. Whoever says יתרו came early also says בני נח brought שלמים, so there is no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was a problem only if someone held both that יתרו came early AND that there were no שלמים before the Torah. The גמרא says no one holds both. The early-יתרו view sides with the opinion that בני נח brought שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of נח did offer שלמים

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether בני נח brought שלמים is tied to when יתרו came. If יתרו came before מתן תורה, his 'זבחים' were שלמים, so בני נח brought שלמים. If he came after, the other view can stand.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יִתְרוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה –
phrases.english: The one who says Yitro came before the giving of the Torah
holds that the descendants of Noach did offer peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יִתְרוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 by linking the יתרו dispute to the שלמים dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even someone who says יתרו came early might hold that בני נח did not bring שלמים, which would leave the question open.
steps.terutzMaskana: The early-יתרו view holds that בני נח brought שלמים, so יתרו's זבחים fit that view.

steps.title: The dispute about יתרו goes back to the תנאים: רבי יהושע's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the question of when יתרו came is an argument between תנאים. רבי יהושע says יתרו came because he heard about the war with עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים. The פסוק says, 'Now יתרו, the priest of מדין, heard.' What news did he hear that made him come and convert? רבי יהושע says: he heard about the war with עמלק, because that story is written right next to it: 'And יהושע weakened עמלק and his people with the edge of the sword.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the argument about when יתרו came already exists among the תנאים. It starts with רבי יהושע's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks what news made יתרו come. רבי יהושע answers: the war with עמלק. That war happened before מתן תורה, and it appears in the פסוקים right before the יתרו story, so in his view יתרו came before מתן תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is like a dispute between the תנאים
Right next to it (in the פסוקים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to step 39. The view that יתרו came before מתן תורה now has a source among the תנאים.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between Tannaim:
phrases.notes: The argument from the last steps about when יתרו came is already found among the earlier sages.

phrases.english: "Now Yitro, the priest of Midian, heard"
phrases.notes: שמות 18:1

phrases.english: What news did he hear
that made him come and convert?
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
He heard about the war with Amalek,
since it is written right next to it:
"And Joshua weakened Amalek
and his people with the edge of the sword."
phrases.notes: שמות 17:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the view in step 39, that יתרו came before מתן תורה, matches a תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: יתרו came after hearing about the war with עמלק, which was before מתן תורה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר המודעי: יתרו heard about מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר המודעי says יתרו came because he heard about מתן תורה. The voice of God at סיני was heard around the whole world, and the kings of the nations trembled and sang.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר המודעי says: he heard about מתן תורה and came. When the תורה was given to ישראל, God's voice went from one end of the world to the other. All the kings of the nations were seized with trembling in their palaces, and they sang a song, as the פסוק says: 'And in His palace all say: Glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second side of the dispute. According to רבי אלעזר המודעי, יתרו came after מתן תורה, because the news he heard was the giving of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר המודעי explains how יתרו, far away in מדין, could have heard about מתן תורה: the voice of God reached the entire world. Even foreign kings in their palaces trembled and sang praise, so the event was impossible to miss.

keyTerms.meaning: The giving of the תורה at סיני

steps.whatToRemember: Two תנאים argue. רבי יהושע says יתרו came after the war with עמלק, before מתן תורה. רבי אלעזר המודעי says he came after מתן תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i says:
He heard about the giving of the Torah [and came],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: for when the Torah was given to Israel
His voice traveled
phrases.notes: "His voice" means the voice of God speaking at סיני.

phrases.english: from one end of the world to the other end,
and all [the kings of] the nations of the world
were seized with trembling in their palaces
and they sang a song,
as it is said:
"And in his palace all say: Glory."
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא's answer to the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר המודעי: יתרו came after hearing about מתן תורה, whose sound reached the whole world.

steps.title: The kings ask בלעם whether a flood is coming
steps.stepSummary: The frightened kings gather around בלעם and ask if the noise means a new מבול. בלעם answers that God already swore never to bring a flood again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They all gathered around בלעם the wicked and said to him: What is this roaring sound we heard? Maybe a flood is coming to the world, as in 'God sat enthroned at the flood'? He said to them: 'God sits as King forever.' The Holy One already swore that He will not bring a flood to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The kings are scared by the noise, so they go to בלעם, their great prophet, to find out what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings read the פסוק 'God sat at the flood' and fear the loud sound means another מבול. בלעם answers from the rest of the same פסוק, 'God sits as King forever.' He explains that God already promised never to send a flood again.

keyTerms.meaning: בלעם the wicked, the prophet of the nations
A flood that destroys the world

phrases.english: They all gathered
around Bilaam the wicked,
and said to him:
What is this roaring sound that we heard?
Perhaps a flood is coming to the world
(he said to them)
phrases.notes: The corrected wording leaves out these words in round brackets. "He said to them" really belongs a bit later, where it shows up in square brackets.

phrases.english: as it says, "God sat enthroned at the flood"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:10

phrases.english: [He said to them:]
"God sits as King forever"
The Holy One, Blessed be He, already swore
that He will not bring a flood to the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר המודעי's description of what happened at מתן תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם tells the kings that God swore never to bring a מבול again.

steps.title: Maybe a flood of fire? בלעם says no
steps.stepSummary: The kings suggest that maybe God will bring a flood of fire instead of water. בלעם answers that God swore not to destroy all flesh in any way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He won't bring a flood of water, but maybe He will bring a flood of fire, as the פסוק says: 'For by fire God will judge.' He said to them: He already swore that He will not destroy all flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The kings push back on בלעם's answer. They suggest that the promise covered only water, and בלעם explains why fire is ruled out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings narrow God's promise: maybe it covered only a flood of water, and a פסוק talks about God judging with fire. בלעם answers that the promise was broader. God swore not to destroy all flesh at all, no matter what the means.

phrases.english: They said to him:
A flood of water He will not bring,
but a flood of fire He may bring,
as it is said:
"For (behold) by fire God will judge."
phrases.notes: ישעיה 66:16. Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: He said to them:
He already swore
that He will not destroy all flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַבּוּל שֶׁל מַיִם אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The kings push back on בלעם's answer, and he explains that the promise is broader.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's promise covers every kind of total destruction, not only water.

steps.title: בלעם explains the noise: God is giving His treasure, the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The kings ask בלעם what the great noise is. He answers that God is giving His precious hidden treasure, the תורה, to His children. The kings respond with a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The kings asked: Then what is this great noise we heard? בלעם said: God has a precious treasure in His storehouse. It was hidden with Him for 974 generations before the world was created, and now He wants to give it to His children, as it says, 'ה׳ will give strength to His people.' Right away all the kings said: 'ה׳ will bless His people with peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי אלעזר המודעי continues. בלעם has ruled out a flood, so the kings ask what the noise really is, and he tells them it is מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 42 and 43 ruled out a flood of water and a flood of fire. Now the real cause is given: God is giving the תורה, which the פסוק calls 'עוז' (strength). This finishes רבי אלעזר המודעי's proof that the whole world heard about מתן תורה, and that is the news that brought יתרו.

keyTerms.meaning: His treasure-house, where precious things are stored away
Strength. Here it is a name for the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר המודעי, the whole world heard מתן תורה. That is what made יתרו come, so in his view יתרו came after מתן תורה.

phrases.english: And what is this tumultuous noise that we heard?
phrases.notes: The kings are speaking. They mean: if it isn't a flood, what is it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: חֶמְדָּה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו,
phrases.english: He said to them: He has a good, precious treasure in His treasure-house,
which was hidden away with Him
for nine hundred seventy-four generations
before the world was created;
and He wants to give it to His children,
as it is said: 'ה׳ will give strength to His people.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:11. The 'strength' here means the תורה.

phrases.english: Immediately they all began and said:
phrases.notes: 'Immediately' is in square brackets because some versions add it.

phrases.english: 'ה׳ will bless His people with peace.'
phrases.notes: The second half of the same פסוק, תהלים 29:11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בלעם dialogue that began in step 42. After the flood ideas are ruled out, the true cause of the noise is revealed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The noise heard around the world was God giving the תורה to Israel. This supports רבי אלעזר המודעי's view that יתרו came because he heard about מתן תורה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: יתרו came because he heard about the splitting of the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר gives a third opinion: יתרו came because he heard about קריעת ים סוף. He supports this with פסוקים in ספר יהושע showing that the nations heard about God drying up water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: יתרו heard about the splitting of the ים סוף and came, as it says, 'And it was, when all the kings of the Amorites heard.' And even רחב the harlot said to the messengers of יהושע: 'For we heard how ה׳ dried up the water of the ים סוף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third תנא's view about what news brought יתרו. רבי אליעזר says it was קריעת ים סוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said מלחמת עמלק and רבי אלעזר המודעי said מתן תורה. רבי אליעזר says קריעת ים סוף, and he shows that miracles of drying up water became famous among the nations. The first פסוק is about the kings hearing of the Jordan drying up. The second, from רחב, mentions ים סוף by name.

keyTerms.meaning: The splitting of the Sea of Reeds
רחב the harlot, who hid יהושע's spies in יריחו

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי אליעזר (this step) with רבי אלעזר המודעי (steps 41–44). They are two different תנאים with two different opinions.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שָׁמַע וּבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He heard about the splitting of the Red Sea and came,
phrases.notes: 'He' is יתרו.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'And it was, when all the kings of the Amorites heard.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:1. The פסוק goes on to say they heard how God dried up the Jordan.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה אָמְרָה לִשְׁלוּחֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: And even Rahab the harlot said to Joshua's messengers:
'For we heard how ה׳ dried up

phrases.notes: יהושע 2:10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third opinion, alongside רבי יהושע (step 40) and רבי אלעזר המודעי (steps 41–44), about what news brought יתרו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יתרו came because he heard about קריעת ים סוף, a miracle that became famous among the nations.

steps.title: Why do two similar verses describe the nations' fear differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares two פסוקים in ספר יהושע. About the Jordan it says 'there was no more spirit in them.' About רחב's words it says 'no more spirit remained in any man.' It asks why the wording is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, where it says 'and there was no more spirit in them,' and what is different here, where it says 'and no more spirit remained in any man'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a small difference in wording between the two פסוקים it just quoted and asks what it means. This step sets up the question; the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jordan פסוק (יהושע 5:1) says 'ולא היה בם עוד רוח.' רחב's words (יהושע 2:11) say 'ולא קמה עוד רוח באיש,' which uses the extra word 'קמה' (remained / stood) and the word 'באיש' (in any man). The גמרא assumes the different wording must teach something and asks what.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A way of asking why two similar cases are treated differently
There / here. Used to point to the two sources being compared
And no more spirit remained (literally, stood up)

phrases.english: What is different there, where it says
phrases.notes: 'There' means the Jordan פסוק. Some versions have the word in round brackets and the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: 'And there was no more spirit in them';
and what is different here, where it says:
'And no more spirit remained in any man'?
phrases.notes: יהושע 2:11, from רחב's words to the spies.
